name: Musau
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Außerfern with a beautiful parish church and an idyllic setting at the foot of the Säuling.
beschreibung:
Musau lies at an elevation of 860 meters in Außerfern, in the district of Reutte, directly on the border with Bayern. The village has around 400 inhabitants and sits at the foot of the striking Säuling, which at 2,059 meters shapes the silhouette of the entire surrounding area. Thanks to its proximity to the German border and to the Lech, Musau is one of the quieter starting points for tours into the Tannheimer Tal or toward Füssen.

The Parish Church of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus in its current form dates from the 19th century and stands out with its slender tower, which rises above the roofs of the small village center. Directly behind the village begins the hiking area on the Säuling: the ascent via the Säulinghütte or the Sulzspitze is popular with mountain hikers, as is the tour to the Frauensee-Hütte with views into the Lechtal. In winter, a small but fine ski touring route on the Vilser Kegel beckons – snowshoers appreciate the untouched slopes around the Pflacherrücken.

In culinary terms, the few inns in the village focus on regional cuisine with cheese from the Lechtal and game dishes from local hunting. Anyone seeking peace, away from the well-known Tiroler hotspots, will find in Musau a village that has preserved its village character – without hustle and bustle, but with direct access to one of the most beautiful mountain landscapes between the Lech and the Ammergauer Alpen. 🏘️
text:
Overview

Musau is situated in the Tyrolean Außerfern at 821 meters above sea level in the picturesque Lech valley, nestled within the Reutte Nature Park Region, approximately six kilometers north of the district capital Reutte and only a few kilometers south of the Bavarian frontier near Füssen. With a population of about 400 residents, Musau is one of the district's most charming and tranquil hideaways. The municipal area spans the left bank of the wild Lech River and comprises the rural hamlets of Brandstatt, Roßschläg, Saba, and Riedle. Musau is framed by the rugged peaks of the Tannheim Mountains, notably the Schartschrofen crags and the 2,238-meter Kellenspitze. Musau stands out for its pristine natural scenery, heartfelt hospitality, and peaceful Alpine atmosphere far removed from mainstream tourist crowds.

History

Settlement in Musau began in the High Middle Ages through forest clearings in the river meadows along the Lech. The village was first documented in 1378 under the name 'Muosaw', an Old German toponym denoting a marshy, moist river meadow. Given its proximity to the Bavarian border and the historic trade route over the Fern Pass, Musau historically played an important role in timber harvesting and log driving along the rushing currents of the Lech. Near the site known as 'Bärenfalle' (Bear Trap), a natural gorge formed a defensive bottleneck in centuries past. The Baroque parish church of the Visitation of Mary (Zu Unserer Lieben Frau Maria Heimsuchung) was erected around 1740 and charms visitors with its balanced architecture and ornate altar paintings. Through centuries of changing times, Musau has preserved its pastoral identity.

Getting There

Musau offers effortless access from both Tyrol and neighboring Bavaria. By car, travelers use the B179 Fernpassstraße to Reutte, continuing onto the L69 regional road straight into Musau. Coming from southern Germany, motorists can arrive toll-free via Füssen and Pinswang across the Weißhaus border crossing in just ten minutes. By train, Musau is exceptionally well served: Musau railway station sits directly on the Außerfern Railway (Außerfernbahn), which runs hourly services connecting Kempten, Pfronten, Reutte, and Garmisch-Partenkirchen. Complementary VVT regional buses serve the hamlets, making green travel without a car completely stress-free.

Tips

A quintessential excursion for hikers and nature enthusiasts is the trek to the traditional Musauer Alm alpine pasture at 1,290 meters in the romantic Raintal valley. The trail ascends through dense mountain forests along crystalline mountain streams to open pastures known for hearty Tyrolean alpine delicacies and magnificent views of the Kellenspitze; further trails continue to the Otto-Mayr-Hütte and Füssener Hütte. River hikers love the world-famous Lechweg trail, which winds directly past Musau and showcases the untamed gravel banks and riparian woodlands of the Nature Park Tiroler Lech. Don't miss the Achsturz, where the wild river rushes through natural rock barriers. In winter, Musau provides quiet winter walking paths, cross-country ski tracks, and tobogganing in the Raintal.
